transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. __. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. It's really nice to meet you, and thank you so much for taking the time to see me today. Um, I guess... well, the main thing that kind of pushed me to finally make an appointment is just some stuff at work. 

I process insurance claims, and I've been having this, I guess, little habit where I just keep getting up from my workstation during the day. It's not like I'm trying to slack off or be a bad employee or anything! It's just... even when I know I’m really supposed to stay put and finish my claim reviews, I find myself walking away from my desk a lot. I hope I'm explaining that right... is that the sort of thing you're asking about?
When you get up from your workstation, is it usually because you feel restless and have trouble staying seated, or because you’re choosing to ignore the rules?

Oh, definitely not choosing to ignore the rules! I promise I really try to be a good employee and do what I'm supposed to. I guess... maybe it is a little bit of restlessness? 

It's actually kind of embarrassing to admit, but, um, like when we have trainings or those longer team meetings, I try so hard to look perfectly focused and professional. But I’ll usually realize I'm bouncing my leg under the table, or clicking my pen, or just shifting around in my chair a whole bunch. I really don't mean to do it, and I try to stop when I notice it, but it just sort of happens even when I'm trying my best to sit still. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm just being difficult or disrespectful to the presenters. Does that kind of answer what you were asking?
Do you notice this same restlessness or difficulty staying seated in other places too, like at home or in social situations?

Um, no, not really. I mean, at home, I'm pretty relaxed. I don't really have that issue when I'm just hanging out in my apartment or, you know, out with friends. I think it's mostly just a work thing, maybe because I want to do a good job so badly and I get a little... antsy? But no, I don't think I have a hard time staying seated anywhere else. I hope that's okay, that it's mostly just happening at the office?
Were you like this when you were a child or teenager, too?

Um, well... I guess if I really think about it, it's not completely out of nowhere. I mean, I was a good kid! I was never a troublemaker or anything like that. But, um, I guess in elementary school, my teachers would sometimes write on my report cards that I was, you know, a bright student, which was nice of them to say. 

But they did sometimes mention that I... well, that I would misplace my worksheets or maybe miss some of the instructions they gave. And I guess I did need a few more reminders than the other kids to actually finish my classwork. It wasn't that I didn't want to do the work, I just... I don't know, things just sort of slipped my mind sometimes. I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a lazy kid, because I really did try my best. Is that the kind of stuff you're looking for?
Have you also had trouble paying attention, staying organized, or finishing tasks in other areas of your life, like at home or in school?

Um, well, I guess... I mean, I really try to keep things together, you know? At home, my apartment isn't, like, perfectly spotless, but it's not a disaster or anything. I try to clean up when I can. And in school... I mean, I did okay. I finished some college, so I definitely got through a lot of my classes. 

I guess maybe I'm not the most organized person in the world, but I don't think it's, like, a huge problem? I mean, I pay my bills and everything. I might just be a little scatterbrained sometimes, but I really do try to stay on top of things. I hope that's a normal amount of, you know, just being a regular person? I don't want you to think my whole life is a mess, because it's really not. Does that make sense?
Do you often feel nervous or worried for no clear reason?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I don't think I'm an overly anxious person or anything. I don't just sit around worrying about nothing. If I get nervous, it's usually because there's a reason for it, like... like a big project at work or something, you know? Just normal stuff that anyone would worry about. I try to stay pretty positive overall. I hope that's a good thing? I definitely wouldn't say I'm nervous for no reason.
Do you have these same attention or restlessness problems in more than one setting, such as at work and at home?

Um, well... I wouldn't really say it's a big *problem* everywhere, you know? Like, at work—I do insurance claims processing—and I mean, the paperwork can be a little repetitive sometimes, so maybe my mind wanders a bit here and there. But I still get my work done! My supervisor hasn't complained or anything, I promise. 

And at home, like I mentioned before, I really try to keep things pretty normal. I definitely don't feel restless or bouncing off the walls or anything like that. I just try to do my best and be responsible wherever I am. I hope I'm answering this right? I just wouldn't say it's some huge issue that follows me around everywhere. Does that make sense?
Do you feel on edge or keyed up much of the time?

Um, no, definitely not. I mean, I don't feel keyed up or on edge at all, really. I like to think I'm a pretty easygoing guy. I don't get all wound up about things, you know? I just try to take life as it comes and stay relaxed. 

I mean, sure, if I have a deadline at work I might feel a little pressure, but nothing crazy. I'm definitely not walking around feeling tense all the time. I try to be pretty chill, honestly. I hope that's what you're looking for? I just don't want you to think I'm some high-strung person, because I'm really not.
Do these attention or restlessness problems cause you noticeable difficulty or impairment in more than one setting, like at work and at home?

Um, no, I wouldn't say they cause, like, noticeable difficulty or... or impairment. That sounds really serious, you know? Like I said, work is fine. I mean, sure, sometimes I might take a little longer to finish a batch of claims because I get distracted by something, but I always get it done. It's not like I'm failing at my job or anything. I'm a hard worker, I really am.

And at home, it's just normal stuff. Maybe I forget to put the laundry in the dryer right away, or I leave a cabinet open, but it's not a big deal. It doesn't ruin my life or anything. I just try to do my best to keep things running smoothly. I'm not impaired, I promise. Is it okay that I don't think it's a huge problem? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right idea.
Before age 12, did you have these kinds of attention or restlessness problems in more than one setting, like at school and at home?

Um, well... I guess if I really think back to when I was a kid... it wasn't totally different, but it wasn't terrible! I mean, I was a good kid, I wasn't causing trouble or anything. 

I remember in elementary school, my teachers would always tell my parents that I was bright and capable. They just... you know, sometimes they'd write on my report card that I lost a worksheet here and there, or maybe I missed some instructions if I was daydreaming a little. And I guess I needed some reminders to finish my classwork sometimes. But I was just a kid, you know? A lot of kids are like that, right? I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a bad student, because I always tried to be good and do what the teacher asked. Does that sound like normal kid stuff to you?
Do you have the same trouble paying attention or staying focused when you're doing activities you enjoy?

Um, no, not really. I mean, if it's something I actually like doing, I can usually focus just fine. Like, I play video games sometimes, or I like to read up on stuff I'm interested in, and I don't really lose track of what I'm doing then. I can pay attention to those things pretty easily. 

I guess... well, sometimes if I'm playing a game for a really long time, I might get a little distracted and want to switch to a different one, but that's just because I want some variety, you know? It's not like I can't pay attention. I just like to mix things up. That's pretty normal, right? I think everyone gets a little bored doing the exact same thing for hours, even if it's fun. So yeah, I'd say I'm pretty good at focusing on things I enjoy. I hope that makes sense?
Do these attention or restlessness problems cause you any real problems at work?

Um... well, I mean, I guess it depends on what you mean by "real problems." Like I said before, I always get my work done eventually, and I'm a really hard worker. But... um... I guess my supervisor did mention something recently. 

It's really not a huge deal, but she... she put me on this sort of performance coaching thing. Just to help me stay on track, you know? Because my claim files were getting a little bit behind, and she had some questions about my accuracy on a few of them. I'm sure it's just a temporary thing to help me improve, right? I just... I really don't want it to mess up my chances for the senior adjuster track I was hoping for. I'm trying really hard to fix it, I promise. Does that sound like the kind of problem you mean, or is that just normal work stuff?
Before age 12, did you have similar attention or restlessness problems at home as well as at school?

Um... well, at home... I don't think it was really a problem, no. I mean, my parents were pretty understanding. 

I guess maybe sometimes my mom would have to ask me a couple of times to clean my room or do my chores, because I'd get kind of wrapped up in playing with my toys or reading a book. But I always did them! I just... maybe needed a little nudge sometimes, like, "Hey, don't forget to take out the trash." But I wasn't, like, running around breaking things or refusing to listen. I was a really good kid at home, I promise. Most kids need to be reminded to do their chores, right? That's just part of growing up, don't you think?
Do these attention or restlessness problems happen in more than one place, like both at work and at home?

Um, I mean... I guess it's mostly just at work where it's noticeable? At home, it's really not a big deal. Like, maybe I'll start folding laundry and then get sidetracked by a text message or something, and the clothes sit on the bed for a while. Or I might misplace my keys now and then. But that's just normal stuff, right? Everyone gets a little scatterbrained at home when they're relaxed. 

My roommate sometimes jokes that I leave half-finished cups of water everywhere, but he's not mad about it or anything. It's not causing any real issues. I just... I like to think I keep things pretty together outside of the office. So I wouldn't say it's a problem in both places. That makes sense, doesn't it? I'm not doing anything too wrong at home, I hope.
Before you were 7 years old, did you already have these attention or restlessness problems?

Um... before I was seven? Gosh, that's really far back. I... I honestly don't remember much from when I was that little. 

I mean, I'm sure I was just a normal kid, you know? Probably playing with blocks or watching cartoons. I don't think my parents or teachers ever said anything about me being restless or not paying attention back then. I was always a pretty quiet, well-behaved little boy, I think. At least, I hope I was! I wouldn't want to think I was a difficult child. So, um, I don't think I had any problems like that before I was seven. Is it okay that I don't really remember much from back then? That's pretty normal, right?
Do these attention or restlessness problems happen in more than one setting, like both at work and at home?

Um, oh, I think we might have just touched on that, right? Or... maybe I didn't explain it very well the first time, I'm sorry! 

But yeah, like I was saying, it's really mostly just at the office where I have a hard time keeping up with all the claims and paperwork. At home, it's honestly fine. I mean, sure, I leave a water glass out here or there, or get a little distracted doing laundry, but I'm definitely not a disaster or anything. I try really hard to be a good roommate and keep things mostly together. 

So, no, I wouldn't say it's a big problem everywhere. Just work, really. Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right answers.
Did you have any of these attention or restlessness symptoms before you were 12 years old?

Um, before twelve? Well, I guess... I mean, looking back, maybe it wasn't completely brand new? 

I don't want to make it sound like I was a bad kid or anything, because I really wasn't! But, um, I guess in elementary school, my teachers would sometimes write on my report cards that I was bright—which is good, right?—but they'd also mention that I, um, lost my worksheets sometimes. Or that I missed instructions when they were talking to the class. 

They said I needed some extra reminders to finish my classwork. But I think a lot of kids are like that, aren't they? Just a little daydreamy? I always tried my best, I promise. It wasn't like I was acting out or trying to be difficult. That's pretty normal for a kid that age, right?
Do you often make careless mistakes when doing work or other tasks that require close attention?

Um, careless mistakes? I mean... I really try not to. I want to do a good job, you know? 

I guess... well, sometimes at work, with the insurance claims, there are just so many little numbers and codes. Every now and then, I might transpose a number or miss a signature box. But I always try to catch it! Or if my supervisor points it out, I fix it right away and apologize. I don't want them to think I don't care, because I really do. 

I wouldn't say I make them *often*... just, you know, a normal amount for someone dealing with a lot of paperwork? I try to be really careful. It's not like I'm just rushing through and making a mess of things. Everyone makes a typo here and there, right? That's not too bad, is it?
Before age 12, were you already having these attention or restlessness problems?

Um, oh, did I... did I not answer that part very well earlier? I'm so sorry if I'm making you repeat yourself! 

But, um, yeah, like I was saying before... looking back, it wasn't completely brand new. I really wasn't a bad kid, I promise! It's just that, in elementary school, my teachers would write on my report cards that I was bright—which is a good thing, right?—but they'd also mention that I, um, lost my worksheets sometimes. Or that I missed instructions when they were talking to the class. 

They said I needed some extra reminders to finish my classwork. But I really always tried my best to be good and do what they asked. I hope that makes sense? I'm trying to give you the right information, I promise.
In the past six months, how often do you have trouble following through on tasks or finishing things once you’ve started them?

Um, following through? I... I don't think I have much trouble with that. I really try to make sure everything gets done. 

I mean, especially at work with the claims, I would never just leave something half-finished. I know people are relying on me, and I don't want to leave my coworkers or the clients in a bind, you know? So if I start a file, I definitely see it through to the end. I want to be dependable. 

I guess at home, maybe I might have a couple of small chores going at the same time, but I always get them done eventually. I wouldn't say I just abandon things. I really do try to finish whatever I start. That's—that's what you're asking, right? I hope I'm explaining that okay.
